title: Fine event timing under shared Mirror phase views
amendment: Initial frozen CPU screen; use actual D1 Vernier acquisition and a compact event Transformer adapter. This does not reproduce the paper's MNIST-pretrained encoder.
scope: Test whether per-window temporal phase coordinates add useful shared-encoder functionality on held-out Vernier offsets while retaining exact timestamp access; do not infer neural-state reuse or broad capacity.

prior_art.PA285: Assa et al., Temporal coding enables hyperacuity in event-based vision, Nature Communications 17, 9951 (2026), DOI 10.1038/s41467-026-76878-6.

hypothesis: A shared event encoder with one small phase coordinate per temporal window will improve sign decoding on unseen Vernier offsets over the same shared encoder without per-window codes, while preserving exact timestamp features and using substantially fewer serialized bytes than four independent encoders.

data.dataset: D1 Vernier event trials from Event-Based Tiny Images, Zenodo record 20973757, datasets/ebtMNIST-D1/Vernier/events.pkl and labels.pkl

windows.selection: first 48 chronological events at or after each start, matching native start-time selection; do not shuffle events

data.label_rule: sign(label-20); report each absolute offset separately
data.split_integrity: Each trial stays whole; its four windows are never split across train/dev/audit. Three optimizer seeds are repeated fits on one acquisition, not independent data worlds.

controls: shared encoder plus official-style fixed periodic sin/cos time features (period 128 ms)
shared encoder plus learned per-window phase coordinate m rotating the periodic sin/cos pair (period 128 ms)
shared encoder plus native per-window time-offset before the same periodic sin/cos encoding (strong exact-affine control)
four independent event encoders, one per temporal window
shared phase-only encoding with the raw timestamp channel removed (timing-loss ablation)
shared exact-time model with timestamp jitter sigma 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2 ms at audit

model.architecture: small pre-norm Transformer encoder: input linear, d_model=32, 1 layer, 4 heads, feedforward=64, mean token pooling, binary sign head
model.normalization: official D1 Vernier input scaling: timestamp ms centered at 110 and scaled by 0.1; x centered at 35; y centered at 26; polarity unchanged
model.training: AdamW, batch 64, maximum 30 epochs, early stop by development accuracy with patience 6; same examples and seed per condition

metrics: actual serialized model payload bytes including m/config/metadata

storage_contract.format: torch.save state dict plus JSON metadata for every method

success_gate: Mirror phase is within 2 percentage points of independent encoders on fresh macro sign accuracy, improves by at least 2 points over shared exact-time, uses <=80% of independent payload bytes, and beats the equal-byte native per-window affine/periodic control by >=2 points without >10% added inference wall time.
failure_gate: The Mirror phase function is exactly represented by the native per-window phase/time-offset control at equal bytes, or it misses any preregistered fresh quality/byte gate. Exact mathematical/native alias is a FAIL for Mirror-specific value even if shared conditioning is useful.
boundaries: No MNIST-pretrained PointTransformer checkpoint is used; this is a small from-scratch mechanism screen, not a reproduction of published Vernier hyperacuity results.
No energy claim; CPU time and token presentations only.
Phase features supplement exact timestamp input except in the declared phase-only ablation.
The independent encoders are a quality upper control; their summed compute is reported.
Fixed phase rotation is mathematically an ordinary time offset in sin/cos coordinates and must not be called a Mirror-specific gain if matched.
